newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle sell $64.50-$65.00 - feedlot.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle sell $64.50-$65.00 - feedlot.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sales near midday Friday were slow at $64.50 to $65.00 per cwt, steady to $0.50 lower than Thursday's active trade, according to feedlot sources and USDA.
Sales were attributed to "clean-up" activity following Thursday's sales at $65.00, down $1.00 from last week.
About 4,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area at $64.50 to $65.00, following weekly movement there of 97,000, according to USDA.
About 1,400 head sold in Kansas at $64.50. Confirmed week to date sales there totalled 85,100 head, USDA said.
A large number of the cattle sold in Kansas were for quick shipment, including next day pick-ups, sources there said.
Weakness was tied to lower beef prices this week and perceptions USDA's Cattle on Feed report later Friday would show a large number of cattle being placed into feedlots during December.

Analysts' December placement estimates averaged 108.2 percent of a year ago, and ranged from 103.0 to 112.0 percent. December marketing estimates averaged 101.8 percent from a range of 99.0 to 107.1 percent. Cattle on-feed supplies as of January 1 averaged 104.2 percent from a range of 102.0-105.0 percent.
